items.name: Chapter 13, Evidence and sourcing
items.stage: Phase 3, round 0, after the fix pass and DR-191’s second pass

reasons.craft: The mapping table’s rules now run whole, the cards sit centered at true size, 13.7 and 13.13 draw through the kit, and patterned lines run solid under their ticks, though the opener sets a numeral inside a quotation (R1).
reasons.clarity: The intro is 73 words and the opener’s grade chip and first typed chip reach the first screen at 1440 px, and the terms I checked (Supplemental Poverty Measure, seasonally adjusted, feasibility, pharmacy benefit managers) are defined at first use.
reasons.brand_fidelity: The opener now carries the evidence chip on the first screen, the line code holds at 2x, and red appears only as Rule 12.5’s target in 13.5, one meaning per view.
reasons.usefulness: Rule 13.4 cites the ten oa.chart.grade tokens by name with their values, which match tokens.json (shortest run 20 widths, 1 px rails, 28 px lead-in), and Rule 13.1 says what a diagram prints in the label’s place.
reasons.evidence_honesty: No plate prints “Official statistic”, 13.9 reads “can raise”, atlas names sit in quotation marks, 13.7 names both groups and one release, and 13.1 prints its margin of error and its estimate’s method, though 13.2’s Documented title states a fact other than its connection’s claim (R2).
reasons.accessibility: Grade travels in pattern, word and the record square, and the phone tables stack readably at 390 px; I did not rerun axe or read the new alt texts, and the editor reports 0 axe violations at both widths.

R1.what: Numeral 1 sits inside the quoted atlas name, “Political spending can ❶ tilt policy toward donors”, so a mark breaks a quotation Rule 13.12 asks to print exactly.
R1.fix: Set the numeral after the closing quotation mark, or before the title with the list naming the verb “can”.

R2.what: The other four rows title the connection’s own claim at its grade. The Documented row’s title, “The Department of Transportation had spent 46.6 percent of the infrastructure law’s transportation funds by July 31, 2026”, states a fact from the record’s evidence, while Connection LE02 claims “Congress decides public investment levels”.
R2.fix: Title the claim in record words, such as “Congress set the infrastructure law’s investment levels in 2021”, and keep the spending figure in the source line.

R3.what: The data lead asks the creative director to choose. In the light-fill variant the named bar stands apart in gray (0.371 against 0.635) and every value prints beside its bar; in view 1 it prints almost like its neighbors (0.371 against 0.386).
R3.fix: Adopt the light fill for the other bars wherever one named bar is emphasized, in red or in ink, and write it into chapter 14’s palette specification in round 5.

KR1.where: S06 in forced colors (Chromium emulation), every hatched cell
KR1.what: The hatch that marks a direction step runs its lines through the cell’s words (“up in reform states”, “up on structure; uncertain on behavior”); at 2x no Canvas halo shows behind the letters.
KR1.fix: In forced colors set each cell’s words on a solid Canvas plate the size of the text block, as labels elsewhere sit on halos, and have the probe test letters against the hatch as well as the fill.

KR2.where: S16 with the drawing 296 px wide, both color modes
KR2.what: The ring key’s last line, “margin of error”, touches the map’s top circles, and several labels sit far from their circles on long leaders (TN, KY, AL and GA below and right of theirs) while ten states go unlabeled.
KR2.fix: At this width move the ring key under the map, and label only circles wide enough to hold their code, listing the rest under the map as the kit already does.

KR3.what: The last tick still reads “40 points”, and West Virginia and Wyoming still set their labels left of their arrows while every other Republican-side label sits right (first review KS5, in part).
KR3.fix: Print the 50 tick the axis now runs to, and keep both labels right of their arrows.

KR4.what: Event dots are about 3 px where Phase 2 drew them near 8 px, and wraps split “P.L. / 119-21” and “Citizens United v. / FEC”.
KR4.fix: Draw the dots at Phase 2’s size, and hold a law number and “v.” with the next word in one no-wrap span, as “H.R. 7008” already is.

KR5.where: S08 with the drawing 296 px wide
KR5.what: The ring around entry RL47 runs 1.5 px past the drawing’s right edge.
KR5.fix: Inset the stack so its ring stays inside the drawing, and let the guard count a ring’s stroke.

weight_recommendation.options_read: The engineer’s “Board 1 weight options”: as it stands 2.954 MB, ask 0.762 MB; chart data compressed 2.796 MB, ask 0.603 MB, no reader loss; tables compressed too 2.141 MB, no ask, every table lost with scripts off; smaller photo copies frees 1.060 MB of the page, no ask, a visible resample of chapter 01’s photographs to 1,200 px wide
weight_recommendation.changes_my_advice: Yes. The photo row did not exist at Part 2, and it frees more than chapter 14 needs without touching a chart, a table or Phase 4.
recommend: Take the smaller photo copies at 1,200 px wide. The page shows them at most 600 px wide, so 1,200 px holds every pixel a 2x screen draws at 100 percent, and a standard screen at 200 percent; only a 2x screen zoomed past 100 percent shows a softer photo. The research lead keeps the originals and their records, updates each SHA-256 and keeps the Corps of Engineers photo’s color profile. It is a visible change, so it needs Dustin’s named approval with the photos shown side by side at true size.
Carry the chart data compressed, which no reader sees (0.158 MB off chapter 14).
Keep every table as live text. I still advise against the tables-compressed row.

Then ask Dustin for no bytes from Phase 4. Raise chapter 14’s stop to the measured figure, about 2.8 MB, paid for by the bytes chapter 01 frees. The page then holds about 0.46 MB of room under 15.5 MB.
Set a budget per finished plate (about 15 KB, today’s measured average) that the build reports each round, since the projection rose from 2.709 to 2.954 MB within this round as notes and words grew.
weight_recommendation.not_tested: I did not see the resampled photographs; the advice rests on the engineer’s measured bytes and the 600 px display width.

risks_for_dustin: Chapter 13 builds at 248,530 bytes of its 250,000 ceiling. Any later word or plate change will pass the ceiling; the editor should cut before adding, and the engineer’s weight pass may free room.
The two new colors, Prussian 56 and 29 percent toward Newsprint, still wait for Dustin’s approval on board 1. I recommend he approve them.
